Units / Layer — Circle Packing

Lay the circular units out inside the pallet footprint to see exactly how many fit per layer — the Total Circles result below drives Units / Layer. When disabled, Units/Row 1 and Units/Row 2 above are used directly.

Reference Photo (Layout Preview disabled)

Attach a photo of the actual packing layout instead — it will appear in the PDF/Excel reports in place of the generated diagram. Enter how many units (boxes or circles) you counted from it, and choose whether that count should drive Units/Layer.

Pallet Footprint & Layout

Auto-filled from Pallet Type above — feel free to override for this product.

Circle Ø is synced live from "Unit Max Diameter" in Calculations Inputs.

Square shapes use the larger of Box Length / Box Width as the side so the unit always fits.

Non-circular units are laid out in a straight grid using the Unit Length & Width entered here (Unit Max Diameter is ignored). Square shapes use the larger of the two values as the side.

Vertical = Box Length runs along the pallet length. Horizontal = every box turned 90°. "Mixed" fills the leftover right/bottom strips with rotated boxes. "Max Optimization" searches every combination for the true maximum. The preview colour-codes each orientation and labels the arrangement.

Adds extra circles beyond the auto-fit grid to use up leftover space. These may slightly cross the inner boundary line (right/bottom only) but will never cross the outer pallet edge.

Bill of Materials (BOM)

Item and Specifications are full dropdown lists — pulled from the Kandil packaging catalogue. Add more choices any time from the "Manage Options" tab. Adjust quantity and unit freely.

"Straps" quantity defaults to the computed Strap Length (m), and "Carton layer" quantity defaults to Layers/Pallet for Full/Half Pallet — or Layers/Pallet ÷ the divisor below for every other Packaging Type (Shrinks, Bulk/Box, Box on FP, Box on HP). Both remain fully editable; edit a quantity directly to stop it from auto-updating (use ↺ to restore the default).

Calculation Settings

These are the engineering constants and core calculation formulas behind the Calculations panel. Tweak any of them and the Spec Sheet recalculates immediately — your changes are saved in this browser.

General constants
Pallet Height add-on (mm)
Shrink Size add-on (mm)
Container max height (mm)
Total height offset — Half Pallet / Box on HP (mm)
Pallet weight base — Full/Half Pallet (kg)
Pallet weight base — other packaging (kg)
Weight allowance — "Other" destination (Ton)
Weight allowance — default destination (Ton)
Total Pallet Height — Half Pallet / Box on HP offset

Total Pallet Height = (Layers/Pallet × Unit Height) × 2 + offset, for Packaging Type = "Half Pallet" or "Box on HP". This offset is now a single flat value (no longer split by Pallet Type) — edit it under General constants below as "Total height offset — Half Pallet / Box on HP (mm)".

Container Type Library — max stack height & weight allowance

Edit any container type's name, max stack height, and (optional) flat weight allowance, or add brand-new container types — they appear immediately in the Container's Type dropdown on the Spec Sheet and as a new column in the Pallet Library table below. Leave Weight Allowance blank to fall back to the Container's Destination based allowance (General constants below), exactly like 40 HC has always worked; 20 FT instead uses a flat cap.

Container TypeMax Stack Height (mm)Weight Allowance (Ton) — blank = use Destination
Pallet Library — dimensions, strap offsets & pallets/container

Edit any pallet's name and size, or add brand-new pallet types — they appear immediately in the Pallet Type dropdown on the Spec Sheet. Length (A) × Width (B) also auto-fill the packing footprint, and Strap Length = ((Pallet Height + A) × 2 × Straps/Side + (Pallet Height + B) × 2 × Straps/Side) ÷ 1000. Pallets/Container has one editable column per Container Type above — exactly like the original 40 HC constants, now extended to every type.

Pallet NameLength A (mm)Width B (mm)Pallets / 40 HCPallets / 20 FT
Core Calculation Formulas

Edit any of the built-in calculation formulas below using the same Excel-style syntax as Custom Calculated Fields. Available variables: all inputs, constants, and the results already computed above in the chain. Errors fall back to the default formula automatically so the rest of the chain never breaks.

Units / Pallet unitsPerPallet

Default: ={unitsPerLayer}*{layersPerPallet}

= 1,995 Unit
Units / Container unitsPerContainer

Default: =IF(OR({isHalfPallet},{isBoxOnHP}),2*{unitsPerPallet}*{palletPerContainer},{unitsPerPallet}*{palletPerContainer})

= 63,840 Unit
Pallet Weight palletWeight

Default: =({unitWeight}*{unitsPerPallet})/1000+{palletWeightBase}

= 449.32 Kg
Pallet Height palletHeight

Default: =({unitHeight}*{layersPerPallet})+{palletHeightClearanceMM}

= 1,189.2 mm
Total Pallet Height totalPalletHeight

Default: =IF(OR({isFullPallet},{isBoxOnFP}),{palletHeight},IF(OR({isHalfPallet},{isBoxOnHP}),({layersPerPallet}*{unitHeight})*2+{totalHeightOffset},0))

= 2,378.4 mm
Container Weight containerWeight

Default: =IF(OR({isFullPallet},{isBoxOnFP}),({palletWeight}*{palletPerContainer})/1000,({palletWeight}*{palletPerContainer}*2)/1000)

= 14.38 Ton
Shrink Size shrinkSize

Default: ={palletHeight}+{shrinkSizeAddOnMM}

= 1,789.2 mm
Strap Length strapLength

Default: =((MAX({strapOffsetA},{strapOffsetB})+{palletHeight})*2*{strapsLongSide}+(MIN({strapOffsetA},{strapOffsetB})+{palletHeight})*2*{strapsShortSide})/1000

= 19.67 m
Height Clearance heightClearance

Default: ={containerMaxHeightMM}-{totalPalletHeight}

= 161.6 mm
Weight Clearance weightClearance

Default: ={weightAllowance}-{containerWeight}

= 5.12 Ton

Saved Products

Products saved here are shared with everyone using this tool, once cloud sync is connected below. Updates from teammates appear live (real-time), with a periodic refresh as a safety net.

☁️ Cloud Sync Setup Connected — synced

This uses Firebase Realtime Database (Google, free tier) — everyone who connects with the same Database URL sees and edits the same shared product list, and changes appear live for everyone else instantly.

1. Go to console.firebase.google.com → Add project (free, just needs a Google account) → skip Analytics if asked.
2. Left sidebar → Build → Realtime Database → Create Database → pick any region → start in test mode.
3. Once created, click the Rules tab and set it to:
{"rules": {".read": true, ".write": true}} → Publish. (This is the same "anyone with the link/value has access" model as before — keep the URL as private as you'd keep a password.)
4. Back on the Data tab, copy the Database URL shown at the top (looks like https://your-project-default-rtdb.firebaseio.com).
5. Paste it below. Anyone who pastes the same URL sees and edits the same shared product list, plus pallet/frame presets (including photos).
